subject: error when use with Skyline for absolute quant

messages.author: ea789c2b76cf441c
messages.subject: error when use with Skyline for absolute quant
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use MsStats through Skyline interface for absolute quantification data by MRM where every native light peptide has a spiked-in heavy isotope labeled standard. I don't have calibration curve done in Skyline and would like to analyze L/H ratio data.
I am getting the "duplicate rows" error message (below).
I've seen this error before for DDA data and removing duplicate peptides/transitions was resolving it.
This time, I created a file with a small set of peptides and samples to troubleshoot where I should not have any duplicate rows and I am still getting this error.

Is there any specific for this type of experiment that I may be missing in settings that causes the duplicate rows error?

When I look at the MsStats data input table created for my data in Skyline, the Light and Heavy peptides are listed separately and the results are given as Area, not L/H ratio. Does this formatting of the data can cause the error?

I'll appreciate suggestions on how to resolve this error.
Thank you!
Anna

messages.subject: Re: error when use with Skyline for absolute quant
parts:
The problem is that you have several replicates that come from the same .wiff file. I guess MSstats does not work with these multi-sample wiff files.

One way to work around this problem would be to change the MSstats Input so that it uses the full path to the file (including the WIFF sample name), instead of just the bare filename.

I have attached a file "DifferentMSstatsInput.skyr" which does this.

The way that you use that .skyr file to replace the MSstats input that the MSstats external tool uses, is to do the following in Skyline:
File > Export > Report
Click the "Edit List" button
In the "Group" dropdown at the top, choose "External Tools"
Click the "Import" button
Choose the file "DifferentMSstatsInput.skyr" that I have attache to this message.
Skyline will ask you if you want to replace the existing "MSstats Input". Say "yes".

After this, the MSstats external tool should work for you, and not give you any errors about duplicate rows.
